interactionStandard.principle: One dominant teaching purpose per screen; low typing load; item-by-item reveal
interactionStandard.teacher: Check · Reset · Show answer · Presentation · Timer · Responses · Live Class / QR

metadata.sourcePolicy: Source-aligned. Delivery format simplified for interaction; no off-book role-model task.

screens.title: AIMS OF THE LESSON
screens.instruction: After the lesson, students will be able to:

groups.heading: 1. Knowledge
items: Identify common personal-information fields, form conventions and abbreviations.
Understand key vocabulary used to describe a local park.

groups.heading: 2. Skills
items: Listen for specific personal details and complete a simple form accurately.
Watch for sequence and key details.
Ask and answer simple questions about a local park.

groups.heading: 3. Attitudes
items: Participate actively in pair and class activities.
Share personal information appropriately and confidently.

screens.title: Medical problem → advice
screens.instruction: Choose one problem. Tell your partner one suitable piece of advice. You do not need to talk about your real health.
screens.question: Which situation would you like to practise?
screens.interactionPrompt: Choose one, then say: ‘I’ve got …’ / ‘You should …’
presentationExpected: I've got a sore throat. — You should drink warm water.
I've got a headache. — You should rest.
I've got a stomach ache. — You should take it easy and seek medical advice if it continues.
I've got a runny nose. — You should rest and drink plenty of water.

screens.title: Warm-up · Forms in everyday life
screens.instruction: Choose one. Then compare your answer with a partner.
screens.question: Which form have you filled in before?
screens.interactionPrompt: Say one piece of information you wrote on it.

screens.title: Which form is it?
screens.instruction: Read the clues. Choose the correct form.

items.question: It asks for passport number, nationality, place of birth and marital status.
It asks about current medications, smoking and details of past surgery.

screens.title: Match form headings with everyday questions
screens.instruction: Work in pairs. Predict each heading, then use Show answer to check one item at a time.

items.question: Are you married, single or divorced?
Do you take any pills or medicine?
How many children do you have?
What country were you born in?
What city or town were you born in?
Who can we call in your family if you need help?
What is the first letter of your middle name?

screens.title: Abbreviations and titles
screens.instruction: Predict the meaning before revealing each answer.

items.question: DOB
No.
e.g.
etc.
Mr / Mrs / Ms / Dr
PLEASE USE CAPITAL LETTERS

screens.title: Track 9 · Part 1: Identity
screens.instruction: Listen once for the situation. Listen again and complete the three details.
screens.example: The receptionist is collecting information from a new patient.

screens.title: Track 9 · Part 2: Contact details
screens.instruction: Listen again. Focus only on the address and contact details.
screens.example: Tip: listen for spelling, numbers and postcode letters carefully.

screens.title: Track 9 · Part 3: Health and exercise
screens.instruction: Listen for key words, not every word.
screens.example: Focus: general health + how often + how long + other exercise.

items.answer: Three times a week — about three hours
Swimming sometimes; walking at weekends with friends

screens.title: Build a new-student form
screens.instruction: Choose the most useful fields for a simple VMMU new-student form. Then compare your choices.
screens.question: Which field is essential on a new-student contact form?
screens.interactionPrompt: After choosing, name three more useful fields from this lesson.

screens.title: Before you watch
screens.instruction: Think for 20 seconds. Then discuss with a partner.
questions: Why do people like going there?

screens.title: Park vocabulary
screens.instruction: Match the key word or phrase to its meaning. Reveal one answer at a time after your pair has decided.

items.question: no matter what
items.answer: It isn't important and it doesn't change my decision.

items.question: pram
items.answer: A four-wheeled vehicle used to move a baby or small child.

items.question: view
items.answer: What you can see around you.

items.question: area
items.answer: A region or part of a town.

items.question: walkway
items.answer: A path or small road only for people.

items.question: blossom

screens.title: Watch 1 · Get the general idea
screens.instruction: Watch without taking notes. Choose the best summary afterwards.
screens.question: What is the video mainly about?
options: How different people use and enjoy a local park
How to build a new park
screens.answer: How different people use and enjoy a local park

screens.title: Watch 2 · Put the scenes in order
screens.instruction: Watch again. Decide the order. Use Show answer only after everyone has finished.

items.question: A woman is walking with her dog.
A man is cycling.
There's a large house near the park.
Two people are walking down a path.
A student is jogging.
A student is doing pull-ups.
A tractor is cutting the grass.

screens.title: Watch 3 · People in the park
screens.instruction: Work in pairs. Listen for one small detail at a time; do not try to write every sentence.

items.question: Woman with dog · How often?
Man at the high part of the park · When?
items.answer: Every day; on sunny days in his lunch break

items.question: Older visitor · Why is the park special?
items.answer: It has happy memories from when the family had children.

items.question: Young visitor · What does the person sometimes do?
Jogger · How often?
items.answer: Quite often / about twice a week

items.question: Final visitor · What does the person like looking at?
items.answer: Wild flowers and blossom on the trees.

screens.title: Role-play · Guess the person
screens.instruction: Student A chooses one person from the video. Student B asks the questions and guesses the person. Then change roles.
support: When do you come to the park?
Why do you like coming here?
Model: A: I come here about twice a week. B: Do you come here to exercise? A: Yes, I do.

screens.title: Exit check · Six quick questions
screens.instruction: Answer briefly. Use this as a final check, not a test.

items.question: What does DOB mean?
Which heading answers: ‘What city or town were you born in?’
What is George's surname?
What does walkway mean?
items.answer: A path or small road only for people

items.question: Which scene comes first in the video ordering task?
items.answer: A woman is walking with her dog.

items.question: Name one question you can ask about someone's park routine.
items.answer: Example: When do you come? / How often do you come? / Why do you like coming here?

screens.title: Homework · Personal information form
screens.instruction: Create a simple form for a new student at VMMU. Include 8–10 useful fields from Unit 1E. Do not enter sensitive real information; use invented or sample details if needed.
screens.label: Required homework
screens.footer: Optional extension: write 4–5 sentences about a local park you know.
